Only 62% had peak activity in the medial prefrontal cortex cluster, while peak activity in the remaining participants was dispersed throughout the prefrontal cortex, including the left lateral prefrontal cortex and left insula.

There was considerable individual variability in the location of the cue-elicited peak activity, suggesting that functional imaging may be useful for tailoring brain-stimulation treatment to individuals.
Men were more likely than women to have a hot spot in the medial prefrontal cortex.

spans.text: Hierarchical clustering analysis revealed that while the majority of the participants had hot spots in the left mPFC, peak activations for the remaining 38% of the individuals were dispersed throughout the prefrontal cortex, including 2 small clusters in the left lateral prefrontal cortex and insula.

source_definition.value: Categorical task-condition term representing blocks of smoking-related cues, neutral cues, and rest.

spans.text: The cue-elicited craving task was based on prior work ( ). Briefly, in the MRI environment participants were exposed to blocks smoking-related (e.g., lighters, packages of cigarettes) and neutral pictures (e.g., pencils, dishes), interleaved with rest blocks.

model_settings.value: Individual voxel-based general linear models assessed relative BOLD signal during smoking cues, neutral cues, and rest. Regressors were convolved with the standard hemodynamic response function. Data were analyzed using SPM5 and custom MATLAB 7.0 scripts after slice-time correction, motion correction, MNI normalization, 8-mm Gaussian smoothing, and 128-s high-pass filtering.

spans.text: For each individual voxel-based analysis was performed using the general linear model to assess relative BOLD signal during periods of smoking cues, neutral cues, and rest. Regressors were convolved with the standard hemodynamic response function.
